#### `slice`

### `metamodel.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Metamodel**

Cross-cutting definitions for all blueprint layers. Provides typed ID refs, versioning, SpecPath, and shared vocabulary. Consumed by all design and governance schema files. Supersedes schemas/blueprint/v1/definitions/metamodel.schema.json.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/metamodel.schema.yaml`_

#### Definitions

#### `versioned_header`

Common header for blueprint documents. Only 'version' required; 'schemaVersion' omitted means latest schema assumed.

**Required:** `version`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → semver` | — |  | Schema definition version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this file belongs to. Enables scoping in multi-context blueprints. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/metamodel.schema.yaml#/$defs/versioned_header`_

#### `entity_properties`

Open metadata bag for entity extensions. Authors may add domain-specific key-value pairs. Known optional keys: term (DDD formal name), definition (formal glossary entry). Custom keys are preserved in the model and available to viewers and generators.

_No declared properties (open or composed object)._

_Source: `schema/v2.7/metamodel.schema.yaml#/$defs/entity_properties`_

#### `code_ref_entry`

Reference to a source code file implementing or reflecting this entity. Path is relative to repository root for same-repo files. For cross-repo files, use URI-style prefix: org/repo#path/to/file. | `role` | `string` | — |  | Purpose of this file relative to the entity. Recommended values: model, interface, implementation, test, validation, migration, configuration, documentation, s… |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Optional clarification of what this file contributes. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/metamodel.schema.yaml#/$defs/code_ref_entry`_

### `migration.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Migration Schema**

Versioned, ordered changes to a blueprint model instance. Enables AS-IS to TO-BE model transformation with traceability and rollback.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/migration.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `migration`, `changes`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this migration conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `migration` | `object` | ✓ |  | Migration identity, lifecycle, and traceability metadata. |
| `changes` | `object` | ✓ |  | Model changes organized by concern: entities (nodes), properties (attributes), relationships (edges), and meta (cross-cutting). At least one change must be pre… |
| `rollback` | `object` | — |  | Rollback feasibility metadata. Automatic rollback derives inverse operations from before/old_value. |

#### Definitions

#### `entity_change`

A change to a whole entity (node in the graph).

**Required:** `kind`, `entity_type`, `target`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `string` | ✓ | `add`, `modify`, `deprecate`, `remove`, `split`, `merge` | Change type: add=new entity, modify=replace, deprecate=mark for removal, remove=delete, split=one to many, merge=many to one. |
| `entity_type` | `string` | ✓ | `concept`, `actor`, `enumeration`, `association`, `operation`, `error` … (47) | Blueprint entity type. Routes validation to the appropriate schema. |
| `target` | `string` | ✓ |  | Entity identifier (typed ref, e.g., CN005, CMD012) or SpecPath. For add: new entity ID. For merge: comma-separated source IDs. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description of this change. |
| `before` | `object` | — |  | Entity state before change. REQUIRED for modify, remove, merge. Enables rollback. |
| `after` | `any` | — |  | Entity state after change. REQUIRED for add, modify, split. For split: array of entities. |
| `reason` | `string` | — |  | Why this specific entity change is needed. |
| `group` | `string` | — |  | Atomic group name. All changes with the same group must apply together or not at all. |
| `order` | `integer` | — |  | Explicit ordering within this migration. Lower numbers apply first. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/migration.schema.yaml#/$defs/entity_change`_

#### `property_change`

A change to individual properties on an existing entity.

**Required:** `kind`, `target`, `property`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `string` | ✓ | `set`, `unset`, `rename`, `append`, `remove-item` | Property operation: set=assign, unset=remove, rename=change name, append=add to array, remove-item=remove from array. |
| `target` | `string` | ✓ |  | Entity identifier (typed ref, e.g., CN005, CMD012). |
| `entity_type` | `string` | — |  | Entity type for validation routing. Same enum as entity_change.entity_type. |
| `property` | `string` | ✓ |  | Property name or dot-path for nested properties (e.g., description, payload.model). |
| `value` | `any` | — |  | New value for set/append operations. Type depends on the property. |
| `old_value` | `any` | — |  | Previous value for conflict detection and rollback. |
| `new_name` | `string` | — |  | New property name for rename operations. |

Design rationale for separate entity status: (1) Questions exist before operations — requirements precede implementation. (2…

Model the questions a bounded context must answer first; an empty `answered_by` is a deliberate gap signal for backlog prioritisation, not an oversight.

### `design/dynamics.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Dynamics**

Design Plane: Runtime concurrency and execution behavior. Covers execution model, parallelism, ordering constraints, race conditions, and resource profiles. Side effects in domain.yaml; observability in quality.yaml; deployment topology in infrastructure.yaml.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/dynamics.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this dynamics document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this dynamics file belongs to. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `execution` | `ref → execution_model` | — |  | Fundamental execution model for this domain's operations. |
| `parallelism` | `array<ref → parallelism_opportunity>` | — |  | Identified opportunities for parallel execution. Each describes operations that can run concurrently, their relationship pattern, and expected benefit. |
| `ordering` | `array<ref → ordering_constraint>` | — |  | Runtime ordering constraints between operations. Defines prerequisites and safe concurrency. Logical/narrative ordering lives in story.schema.yaml. |
| `race_conditions` | `array<ref → race_condition>` | — |  | Known concurrency hazards and mitigations. Proactive documentation of races prevents production incidents. |
| `resources` | `ref → resource_profile` | — |  | Resource consumption characteristics: memory, I/O, and CPU profiles for capacity planning. |

#### Definitions

#### `execution_model`

High-level declaration of how operations are scheduled and coordinated. Specific parallelism and ordering details are in their respective collections.

**Required:** `model`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `string` | ✓ | `sequential`, `parallel`, `actor`, `csp`, `reactive`, `event-driven` … (7) | Primary execution model: sequential=one-at-a-time, parallel=concurrent, actor=message-passing, csp=communicating processes, reactive=event-stream, event-driven… |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Narrative description of the execution approach. |
| `rationale` | `string` | — |  | Why this execution model was chosen. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/dynamics.schema.yaml#/$defs/execution_model`_

#### `parallelism_opportunity`

An identified opportunity to run operations concurrently. Documents relationship pattern, expected benefit, and implementation complexity.

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `operations`, `relationship`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → parallelism_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique parallelism identifier (PAR + NNN). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Human-readable name (e.g. 'Parallel inventory scanning'). |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings. |
| `operations` | `array<ref → operation_ref>` | ✓ |  | Operations that can run concurrently in this opportunity. |
| `relationship` | `string` | ✓ | `independent`, `embarrassingly-parallel`, `pipeline`, `fork-join`, `scatter-gather` | Concurrency pattern: independent=no dependencies, embarrassingly-parallel=same op on partitioned data, pipeline=concurrent stages, fork-join=fan out then merge… |
| `benefit` | `string` | — |  | Expected benefit (e.g. '2-3x speedup on multi-core systems'). |
| `complexity` | `string` | — | `low`, `medium`, `high` | Implementation complexity: low=trivial, medium=requires synchronization, high=complex coordination. |
| `implemented` | `boolean` | — |  | Whether this parallelism is currently implemented. false=identified opportunity, not yet realized. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

#### `ordering_constraint`

Runtime ordering constraint between operations. Absorbs v1 execution_order and can_parallel_with. This is runtime sequencing; logical/narrative ordering is in story.schema.yaml.

| `enables` | `array<ref → operation_ref>` | — |  | Operations that become eligible AFTER these operations complete. |
| `can_parallel_with` | `array<ref → operation_ref>` | — |  | Operations that may execute concurrently. Explicitly marks safe concurrency. Moved from v1 operations schema. |
| `step` | `integer` | — |  | Optional step number for sequential planning. Operations sharing a step may run in parallel if parallel=true. Lower numbers execute first. |
| `parallel` | `boolean` | — |  | Whether operations within this step can run in parallel. Only meaningful when step is provided. |
| `condition` | `string` | — |  | Optional condition under which this ordering applies (e.g. 'only in batch mode'). |
| `note` | `string` | — |  | Additional context about this ordering constraint. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

**Blueprint UI**

### `design/quality.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Quality**

Design Plane: Non-functional requirements as first-class entities. Covers metrics, KPIs, SLOs, SLAs, security, compliance, resilience, and observability. Traceability chain: goal→KPI→metric→operation/concept→SLO→SLA.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/quality.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this quality document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this quality file belongs to. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `metrics` | `array<ref → metric>` | — |  | Quantitative measurements of system behavior. Foundation for KPIs, SLOs, and observability — define what you measure before defining targets. |
| `kpis` | `array<ref → kpi>` | — |  | Key Performance Indicators — metrics with business targets. Link operational measurements to strategic goals from motivation.schema.yaml. |
| `slos` | `array<ref → slo>` | — |  | Service Level Objectives — operational reliability targets the engineering team commits to. Based on metrics, constrain operations. |
| `slas` | `array<ref → sla>` | — |  | Service Level Agreements — external contractual commitments built on SLOs. Carry business consequences (penalties, credits) when breached. |
| `security` | `array<ref → security_requirement>` | — |  | Security requirements governing operations and data: authentication, authorization, encryption, access control, audit. |
| `compliance` | `array<ref → compliance_requirement>` | — |  | Regulatory, privacy, and data retention requirements. Links concepts to the regulations that govern them. |
| `resilience` | `array<ref → resilience_requirement>` | — |  | Availability, disaster recovery, and backup requirements. Defines RTO, RPO, and failover strategies. |
| `findings` | `array<ref → finding>` | — |  | AS-IS internal-quality defects discovered in the codebase (maintainability / modularity dimension of ISO/IEC 25010): smells, duplication, drift, coupling, boun… |
| `observability` | `object` | — |  | Observability strategy across four pillars: metrics, logs, traces, events. Each pillar is optional — start with what you need. |

#### Definitions

#### `metric`

A quantitative measurement of system behavior. Metrics are the foundation of all quality management.

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `type`, `unit`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → metric_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique metric identifier (MT + NNN). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Human-readable metric name (e.g. 'Order Processing Latency'). |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings. |
| `type` | `string` | ✓ | `latency`, `throughput`, `availability`, `error-rate`, `saturation`, `business` … (7) | Metric category: latency=time-to-complete, throughput=processing rate, availability=uptime, error-rate=failure rate, saturation=resource utilization, business=… |
| `unit` | `string` | ✓ |  | Unit of measurement (e.g. 'ms', 'req/s', '%', 'orders/hour'). |
| `measures` | `object` | — |  | Blueprint entities this metric observes. Links measurement to domain model. |
| `collection` | `object` | — |  | How this metric is gathered. Optional — useful for implementation planning. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Metric version for lifecycle tracking. |

#### `finding`

An AS-IS internal-quality defect discovered in the codebase (maintainability / modularity): a smell, duplication, drift, coupling, boundary leak, god-class, or dead/dual implementation. An ASSESSMENT of current state — not a target. Carries code_refs to the offending code and `affects` refs to the domain entities it touches. Anchors the remediation chain: finding → risk → decision → migration (th…

| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings. |
| `kind` | `string` | ✓ | `god-class`, `duplication`, `drift`, `coupling`, `boundary-leak`, `misplaced-shared-kernel` … (12) | Defect category: god-class=one class, many concerns; duplication=repeated logic/model; drift=divergent parallel implementations; coupling=undue dependency; bou… |
| `quality_characteristic` | `ref → quality_characteristic` | — |  | ISO/IEC 25010:2011 top-level product-quality characteristic this finding degrades — the top-level attribute only (finer grain goes in `quality_subcharacteristi… |
| `quality_subcharacteristic` | `ref → quality_subcharacteristic` | — |  | ISO/IEC 25010 sub-characteristic under `quality_characteristic` (e.g. `modularity` under `maintainability`, `confidentiality` under `security`). Consistency wi… |
| `regulatory` | `array<string>` | — |  | Regulatory frameworks this finding relates to (e.g. GDPR, PCI-DSS, WCAG). A tag, NOT a quality characteristic — regulatory concerns classify as security / func… |
| `severity` | `string` | ✓ | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | How damaging the defect is to the relevant quality characteristic / the modernization goal. |
| `effort` | `string` | — | `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` | Rough remediation effort (t-shirt size). Optional. |
| `statement` | `string` | ✓ |  | The observation — what is wrong and where, in plain language. |
| `recommendation` | `string` | — |  | Suggested remediation direction, in prose. The structured fix lives in the linked migration. |
| `affects` | `object` | — |  | Blueprint entities this finding touches. Links the defect to the domain model. |

| `certainty` | `ref → certainty` | — |  | Confidence that this is a real defect (not a false positive). Optional. |
| `discovery_stage` | `ref → discovery_stage` | — |  | Epistemic maturity of this finding. Optional. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Finding version for lifecycle tracking. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Finding-level ownership override. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |

### `design/rules.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Rules**

Design Plane — Layer 2: Business rules. Structural invariants, classification, derivation, equivalence, validation, and state-transition rules with SBVR modality.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/rules.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this document. Bump major for removed/renamed rules, minor for new rules, patch for logic clarifications. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this file belongs to. When set, all rule IDs are addressable as scope.ID from outside. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `structural` | `array<ref → rule>` | — |  | Invariant rules that must always hold true. Express fundamental domain constraints that cannot be violated. |
| `classification` | `array<ref → rule>` | — |  | If-then categorization rules that classify domain entities into categories based on conditions. |
| `derivation` | `array<ref → rule>` | — |  | Rules defining how values are computed or derived from other concept properties. |
| `equivalence` | `array<ref → rule>` | — |  | Rules defining when two concepts or values are considered equivalent for domain purposes. |
| `validation` | `array<ref → rule>` | — |  | Input validation rules applied at system boundaries, checking external data before it enters the domain. |
| `transition` | `array<ref → transition_rule>` | — |  | State transition rules defining when and how concepts may move between lifecycle states. Referenced by concept transition_rules[]. |

#### Definitions

#### `rule`

Business rule. Minimum: id, name.

**Required:** `id`, `name`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → rule_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique rule ID. Prefix indicates category: SR=structural, CR=classification, DR=derivation, EQ=equivalence, VR=validation. |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Human-readable name in imperative form. Describes what the rule enforces, not how. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description of what the rule does and why. |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary (≤200 chars) for listings and quick reference. Must be self-contained. |
| `logic` | `ref → logic_tuple` | — |  | Business logic as when/then/else. 'when' = condition (omit for invariants). 'then' = required outcome. 'else' = alternative. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Rule version for individual lifecycle tracking. |
| `modality` | `ref → sbvr_modality` | — |  | Deontic strength: necessary=domain truth, obligatory=system enforced, prohibited=must never happen, permitted=explicitly allowed. |
| `concepts` | `array<ref → concept_ref>` | — |  | Concepts this rule constrains or references. Enables traceability from rules to domain vocabulary. |
| `fact` | `string` | — |  | Structured predicate anchoring the rule to concept properties. Optional; supplements human-readable logic. Example: 'Inventory.entries.count > 0'. |
| `rationale` | `string` | — |  | Why this rule exists and what business need it serves. |
| `scope` | `string` | — |  | Applicability scope within the domain (e.g. input-validation, post-processing). Narrows when/where rule applies. |
| `certainty` | `string` | — | `definitive`, `heuristic` | Whether rule is absolute (definitive) or probabilistic (heuristic). Heuristic rules may produce false positives. |
| `examples` | `array<object>` | — |  | Input/output pairs demonstrating the rule in action. |
| `on_violation` | `ref → violation_response` | — |  | Response when this rule is violated. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Rule-level ownership override. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |
| `provenance` | `ref → provenance` | — |  | Epistemic provenance for this rule (brownfield modeling confidence). Distinct from rule.certainty (definitive\|heuristic). |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/rules.schema.yaml#/$defs/rule`_

#### `transition_rule`

State transition rule. Defines when and how a concept moves between lifecycle states.

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `concept`, `from`, `to`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → transition_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique transition rule ID (e.g. TR001 or billing.TR001). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Human-readable name for this transition. |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary of the state transition (≤200 chars). |
| `concept` | `ref → concept_ref` | ✓ |  | The concept whose lifecycle state machine this transition belongs to. Must define states[]. |
| `from` | `string` | ✓ |  | Source state name. Must match a state defined in the referenced concept's states[]. |
| `to` | `string` | ✓ |  | Target state name. Must match a state defined in the referenced concept's states[]. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Transition rule version for lifecycle tracking. |
| `guard` | `object` | — |  | Precondition that must be true for this transition to occur. |
| `fact` | `string` | — |  | Structured predicate for the guard condition. Example: 'Order.items.all(validated) AND Order.payment.authorized'. |
| `modality` | `ref → sbvr_modality` | — |  | Deontic strength for this transition. |
| `rationale` | `string` | — |  | Why this transition exists in the domain lifecycle. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description of this transition. |
| `on_violation` | `ref → violation_response` | — |  | Response when an invalid transition is attempted. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Transition rule-level ownership override. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |
| `provenance` | `ref → provenance` | — |  | Epistemic provenance for this transition rule (brownfield modeling confidence). |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/rules.schema.yaml#/$defs/transition_rule`_

#### `violation_response`

Response when a rule is violated. Grouped by severity: hard-stop, soft-continue, deferred, recovery.

**Required:** `action`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `string` | ✓ | `exit`, `throw`, `reject`, `show-usage-and-exit`, `warn`, `warn-and-skip` … (12) | Violation action. Hard-stop: exit, throw, reject, show-usage-and-exit. Soft: warn, warn-and-skip, log, degrade. Deferred: queue-for-review, escalate, quarantin… |
| `code` | `integer` | — |  | Exit/error code for exit, throw, or reject actions. |
| `message` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description of the violation. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/rules.schema.yaml#/$defs/violation_response`_

### `design/story.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Story**

Design Plane — Layer 4: Domain stories expressing logical operation sequences, actor interactions, and side effects. Ordering here is logical; runtime ordering is in dynamics.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/story.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `name`, `version`, `stories`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Domain or service name these stories belong to. |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this story document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this story file belongs to. |
| `stage` | `string` | — |  | Development stage (e.g. draft, review, approved). |
| `domains` | `object` | — |  | Domain references used in these stories (name → identifier mapping). |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `stories` | `array<ref → story>` | ✓ |  | Domain stories describing how operations flow from trigger to outcome. |
| `user_stories` | `array<ref → user_story>` | — |  | Agile user stories — PRD building blocks capturing user-level goals. |
| `use_cases` | `array<ref → use_case>` | — |  | Use cases — scenario-level requirements. Supports functional and journey modes. |

#### Definitions

#### `story`

A domain story: named narrative of actor-operation collaboration.

**Required:** `id`, `title`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → story_ref` | ✓ |  | Typed story identifier (STR### pattern). |
| `title` | `string` | ✓ |  | Story title in imperative or actor-goal form. |
| `storyUri` | `string` | — |  | Optional URI to the story source (e.g. Jira, Linear, GitHub issue). |
| `status` | `string` | — |  | Story status (e.g. draft, approved, implemented). |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Narrative description of this story's context and goal. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `initiated_by` | `array<ref → actor_ref>` | — |  | Optional list of actor refs that can initiate this story (human, system, or time). Used for Event Storming lane-start actor stickies. |
| `activities` | `array<ref → story_activity>` | — |  | Process activities composing this story. Each activity is an asynchronous phase containing synchronous steps. |
| `process` | `object` | — |  | Process metadata when this story represents a business process. Enables BPMN generation. When absent, story is a lightweight interaction sequence. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Story-level ownership override. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/story.schema.yaml#/$defs/story`_

#### `story_activity`

Process activity within a story. Entry point into domain causal chain (produces/reacts_to).

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `entry_operation`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → story_activity_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique activity identifier (SA001, SA002, etc.). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Human-readable activity name describing this process phase. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Detailed description of what this activity accomplishes. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `entry_operation` | `ref → operation_ref` | ✓ |  | Domain operation where this activity begins. Generator follows causal chain (produces/reacts_to) from here. |
| `triggered_by` | `array<union>` | — |  | What initiates this activity: an actor (for first activity) or an event operation (for reactive activities). |
| `steps` | `array<object>` | — |  | Optional convenience view of operations in this activity — not source of truth. Domain causal links (produces/reacts_to) are authoritative. Validator WARNS if… |
| `next_activities` | `array<ref → story_activity_ref>` | — |  | Optional explicit links to subsequent activities. When absent, flow is inferred from domain causal links. |
| `path_type` | `string` | — | `happy`, `error`, `compensation` | Process path classification: happy=expected flow, error=exception handling, compensation=rollback/undo. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/design/story.schema.yaml#/$defs/story_activity`_

#### `user_story`

| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings and PRD tables. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Additional context or acceptance narrative. |

| `release_target` | `ref → release_target` | — |  |  |
| `story_points` | `integer` | — |  | Relative effort estimate for sprint planning. |

| `test_cases` | `array<ref → test_ref>` | — |  | Test cases validating this story. |

Use case — a scenario-level requirement describing actor interaction with the system. Serves as both functional specification (steps with operations) and user journey (steps with screens, emotions, pain points). Groups user stories and optionally references implementing stories (STR###).

## Governance Plane

<a id="governance-capability"></a>

### `governance/capability.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Business Capabilities**

Governance Plane: Business Capability Map — a hierarchical view of what the business can do, independent of organizational structure or process. Capabilities are stable building blocks mapping the business 'what' (not 'how' or 'who'). Reference operations, rules, and concepts for traceability.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/capability.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`, `capabilities`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this capability document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context or business domain this capability map covers. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `capabilities` | `array<ref → capability>` | ✓ |  | Top-level business capabilities. Level 1 capabilities decompose into level 2 via nested children, level 2 into level 3, etc. Typical maps have 2-3 levels. |

#### Definitions

#### `capability`

A business capability — something the business can do or needs to do. Stable and technology-independent. Links to operations (how), rules (constraints), and concepts (domain vocabulary).

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `level`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → capability_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique capability identifier (CAP + NNN). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Capability name in business language (e.g. 'Order Management', 'Payment Processing'). |
| `level` | `integer` | ✓ |  | Hierarchy level: 1=top-level business capability, 2=decomposition of level 1, 3=further decomposition. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | What this capability means in business terms. Describe the 'what' without implementation details. |
| `children` | `array<ref → capability>` | — |  | Sub-capabilities that decompose this capability. Each child is a full capability with its own ID and optional further children. |
| `operations` | `array<ref → operation_ref>` | — |  | Operations that implement this capability. Links business 'what' to domain 'how'. |
| `rules` | `array<ref → rule_ref>` | — |  | Rules that govern this capability. |
| `concepts` | `array<ref → concept_ref>` | — |  | Domain concepts involved in this capability. |
| `goal_refs` | `array<ref → goal_ref>` | — |  | Strategic goals this capability supports. |
| `maturity` | `string` | — | `emerging`, `developing`, `established`, `optimized` | Current maturity: emerging=not yet implemented, developing=partially built, established=fully operational, optimized=continuously improved. |
| `strategic_importance` | `string` | — | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | Business strategy importance: critical=core differentiator, high=essential, medium=supporting, low=commodity. |
| `delivery_priority` | `ref → delivery_priority` | — |  | MoSCoW delivery priority. Orthogonal to strategic_importance: a high-importance capability may be wont-have for current release. |
| `owner` | `string` | — |  | Actor responsible for this capability (use actor_ref ACTnnn for traceability). |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Capability version for lifecycle tracking. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Capability-level ownership override. |
| `value_stream_refs` | `array<ref → value_stream_ref>` | — |  | Value streams this capability participates in (convenience back-reference; authoritative direction is value_stream → stages[].capabilities[]). |
| `discovery_stage` | `ref → discovery_stage` | — |  | Epistemic maturity of this capability. |
| `certainty` | `ref → certainty` | — |  | Confidence level of this capability assessment. |
| `evidence` | `ref → evidence` | — |  | Evidence justifying this capability's assessment. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/capability.schema.yaml#/$defs/capability`_

<a id="governance-decisions"></a>

### `governance/decisions.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Decisions**

Governance Plane: Architecture Decision Log (ADR). Chronological, append-only record of design decisions with typed impact references, motivation traceability, and change-set analysis.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`, `decisions`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version. Bump minor for new decisions, patch for status updates. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this decisions file belongs to. Enables filtering in multi-context blueprints. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `decisions` | `array<ref → decision>` | ✓ |  | Architecture Decision Log. Chronological, append-only. Each entry is immutable once landed — supersede rather than modify. |
| `business_decisions` | `array<ref → business_decision>` | — |  | Bounded Context Canvas v5 business decisions (BD###). Distinct from `decisions[]` above: business_decisions are high-level policy statements governing a bounde… |

#### Definitions

#### `decision`

An Architecture Decision Record (ADR). Minimum: id, title, summary, date, status, rationale.

**Required:** `id`, `title`, `date`, `status`, `rationale`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → decision_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique decision ID (e.g. D001 or billing.D001). Assigned chronologically; never reused. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description. |
| `title` | `string` | ✓ |  | Short descriptive title understandable without reading the full rationale. |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings and quick scanning (≤200 chars). Self-contained. |
| `date` | `string` | ✓ |  | Date proposed or accepted. Format: YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `status` | `ref → decision_status` | ✓ |  | Lifecycle status: proposed→accepted→landed; rejected or deprecated at any stage. |
| `rationale` | `ref → rationale` | ✓ |  | The reasoning behind this decision. Answers 'why' for future readers. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Decision version for individual lifecycle tracking. |
| `decision_scope` | `string` | — |  | Context, component, or SpecPath prefix this decision applies to (e.g. billing, billing.rules, order-api). |
| `motivation_refs` | `ref → motivation_links` | — |  | Motivation entities driving this decision: goals served, risks mitigated, assumptions, trade-offs accepted. |
| `capability_refs` | `array<ref → capability_ref>` | — |  | Business capabilities this decision supports or enables. |
| `change_set` | `array<ref → change_item>` | — |  | Machine-readable manifest of changes introduced. Each entry describes one blueprint element change. |
| `declared_impact` | `ref → impact_declaration` | — |  | Author's declaration of affected blueprint entities. Direct changes plus transitive ripple hints. |
| `consequences` | `object` | — |  | Known consequences of this decision: positive benefits and negative costs or technical debt. |
| `acceptance` | `ref → acceptance_criteria` | — |  | Conditions that must be met for this decision to be considered fully implemented. |
| `links` | `ref → decision_links` | — |  | External references: issue tracker, PRs, docs, and decision chain (supersedes/superseded_by). |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Decision-level ownership override. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |
| `discovery_stage` | `ref → discovery_stage` | — |  | Epistemic maturity of this decision. Proposed decisions are typically hypothesis or exploring. |
| `certainty` | `ref → certainty` | — |  | Confidence level of this decision. Speculative for proposed, confirmed for landed. |
| `evidence` | `ref → evidence` | — |  | Evidence chain justifying this decision — benchmarks, experiments, stakeholder feedback. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/decision`_

#### `rationale`

The reasoning behind a decision: problem context, options explored, chosen approach.

**Required:** `problem`, `chosen`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `problem` | `string` | ✓ |  | The problem or question that prompted this decision. Describes context and constraints. |
| `options` | `array<union>` | — |  | Alternative approaches considered before choosing. Items can be plain strings (backward compatible) or structured objects with pros/cons analysis for ADR gener… |
| `chosen` | `string` | ✓ |  | The option selected and why it was preferred over alternatives. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/rationale`_

#### `motivation_links`

Traceability from decision to motivation layer: what goals, risks, assumptions, and trade-offs drove it.

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `goals` | `array<ref → goal_ref>` | — |  | Goals this decision serves or advances. |
| `risks` | `array<ref → risk_ref>` | — |  | Risks this decision mitigates. |
| `assumptions` | `array<ref → assumption_ref>` | — |  | Assumptions this decision depends on being true. |
| `trade_offs` | `array<ref → trade_off_ref>` | — |  | Trade-offs this decision consciously accepts. |
| `questions` | `array<ref → question_ref>` | — |  | Domain competency questions (QN###) that drove this decision. |
| `inquiries` | `array<ref → inquiry_ref>` | — |  | Governance inquiries (INQ###) that drove or are resolved by this decision. Distinct from questions — inquiries are temporary governance concerns, questions are… |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/motivation_links`_

#### `change_item`

A single change introduced by a decision. Blueprint element change with versioning impact.

**Required:** `kind`, `target`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `ref → change_kind` | ✓ |  | Change type: add→minor, modify→minor/major, deprecate→minor, remove/rename/split/merge→major. |
| `target` | `ref → spec_path` | ✓ |  | SpecPath to the affected blueprint element (e.g. rules.classification.CR003). |
| `before` | `string` | — |  | State before the change (snapshot or description). Required for modify/remove. |
| `after` | `string` | — |  | State after the change (snapshot or description). Required for add/modify. |
| `semver` | `ref → semver_impact` | — |  | Versioning impact of this specific change. |
| `notes` | `string` | — |  | Explanation of why this change is needed. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/change_item`_

#### `impact_declaration`

Author's declaration of affected entities: direct changes and transitive ripple hints.

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direct` | `object` | — |  | Entities directly changed by this decision. |
| `transitive_hints` | `array<string>` | — |  | Human hints about expected ripple effects beyond direct impacts. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/impact_declaration`_

#### `acceptance_criteria`

Conditions for this decision to be considered fully implemented. Free strings for low barrier.

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `must_pass_tests` | `array<string>` | — |  | Tests that must pass (names or free strings). |
| `new_tests_to_add` | `array<string>` | — |  | New tests that need to be created. |
| `docs_to_update` | `array<string>` | — |  | Documentation that needs updating. |
| `reviews_required` | `array<string>` | — |  | Reviews or approvals needed before landing. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/acceptance_criteria`_

#### `decision_links`

External references and decision chain links.

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `issues` | `array<string>` | — |  | Issue tracker references (URLs or IDs). |
| `prs` | `array<string>` | — |  | Pull request references. |
| `docs` | `array<string>` | — |  | Documentation references. |
| `supersedes` | `array<ref → decision_ref>` | — |  | Decisions this one replaces. Array supports many-to-one merge (multiple old decisions consolidated). |
| `superseded_by` | `array<ref → decision_ref>` | — |  | Decisions that replace this one. Array supports one-to-many split (one decision divided). |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/decision_links`_

#### `option`

A structured decision option with description, pros, cons, and open questions. Used for ADR generation with full analysis per alternative.

**Required:** `name`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Short name of the option (e.g. 'x-vector voice conversion', 'McAdams coefficient'). |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Detailed description of the option — technical approach, constraints, prerequisites. |
| `pros` | `array<string>` | — |  | Advantages of this option. Each item is a self-contained benefit statement. |
| `cons` | `array<string>` | — |  | Disadvantages, risks, or costs of this option. Each item is a self-contained concern. |
| `open_questions` | `array<string>` | — |  | Unresolved questions that must be answered before this option can be chosen. |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/option`_

#### `business_decision`

BCC v5 Business Decision — a key rule or policy that governs the behaviour of one or more bounded contexts. NOT a data-level invariant (those live in rules.schema.yaml as Rule); NOT an ADR (D### above). These are higher-level policy statements expressing "what we will / will not do" in the bounded context's domain.

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `description`, `bounded_context_ref`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → business_decision_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique business decision identifier (e.g. BD001 or orders.BD001). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Short human-readable name. Used in displayId fallback when no context prefix is set. |
| `description` | `string` | ✓ |  | Full statement of the decision. Free text; may be multi-paragraph. |
| `bounded_context_ref` | `ref → context_prefix` | ✓ |  | Owning bounded context (kebab-case context name). A single decision may apply to multiple contexts via linked_contexts[]. |
| `linked_contexts` | `array<ref → context_prefix>` | — |  | Other contexts this decision affects (cross-context policy). |
| `linked_user_stories` | `array<ref → user_story_ref>` | — |  | User stories that motivated this decision. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Decision version for individual lifecycle tracking. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Entity-level ownership override. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/decisions.schema.yaml#/$defs/business_decision`_

<a id="governance-leverage"></a>

### `governance/leverage.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Leverage Map**

Governance Plane: Leverage Map — the prioritization tier that sits ABOVE the AS-IS remediation chain (finding → risk → decision → migration). A leverage point (LP###) is the "vital few" cross-cutting intervention: it bundles the findings/risks/decisions/fitness-functions it addresses, projects the consequences of acting (or not), and delegates its delivery/sequencing to roadmap work-items (WI###) rather than re-modelling execution. Answers: what are the highest-leverage things to do, in what or…

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/leverage.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`, `leverage_points`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this leverage map. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context / slice this leverage map covers (omit for a systemic, root-level map). |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Leverage points inherit unless overridden. |
| `horizon` | `string` | — |  | Planning horizon this map targets (e.g. 'H2-2026', 'next 2 quarters'). Free-text. |
| `ranking_basis` | `array<string>` | — |  | The shared rubric used to rank leverage points (e.g. urgency, dependency-hub, blast-radius, delivery-risk-reduction, evidence-confidence). Documents HOW `rank`… |
| `pareto_core` | `array<ref → leverage_ref>` | — |  | The committed 'vital few' — a CURATED subset of leverage points the team commits to now. Semantically distinct from `rank` (which orders all points): pareto_co… |
| `leverage_points` | `array<ref → leverage_point>` | ✓ |  | The leverage points — prioritized cross-cutting interventions. |
| `watchlist` | `array<ref → watch_item>` | — |  | Signals being MONITORED but not yet acted on — candidate future leverage points or deferred risks. Lightweight: enough to not lose the thread, without promotin… |

#### Definitions

#### `leverage_point`

A prioritized cross-cutting intervention — "the one thing to do for X". Synthesizes the model: it references (does NOT duplicate) the findings/risks/decisions/fitness-functions it addresses, the migrations/roadmap-work-items that deliver it, and the goals/value-streams it advances. Caps the remediation chain finding → risk → decision → migration with a prioritization tier. Connected to decisions…

**Required:** `id`, `title`, `one_thing`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → leverage_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique leverage-point identifier (LP + 3 digits, optional context prefix). |
| `title` | `string` | ✓ |  | Short imperative title of the intervention (e.g. 'Isolate reporting workloads from the interactive path'). |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings (≤120 chars). |
| `one_thing` | `string` | ✓ |  | The single highest-value thing this intervention achieves, in prose. The definitional core: if you did only one thing here, this is it (e.g. 'make schema evolu… |
| `rank` | `integer` | — |  | Priority rank (1 = highest). Assigned per `ranking_basis`. Optional. |
| `area` | `string` | — |  | Concern area this intervention sits in (e.g. 'delivery-data', 'domain-architecture', 'platform'). Free-text label for grouping. |
| `status` | `string` | — | `proposed`, `accepted`, `in-progress`, `realized`, `superseded`, `dropped` | Lifecycle: proposed=logged, accepted=committed, in-progress, realized=done, superseded=replaced, dropped=won't do. |
| `finding_refs` | `array<ref → finding_ref>` | — |  | AS-IS quality findings (FN###) this intervention remediates. |
| `risk_refs` | `array<ref → risk_ref>` | — |  | Motivation risks (R###) this intervention mitigates. |
| `decision_refs` | `array<ref → decision_ref>` | — |  | Decisions (D###) this intervention bundles / is realized through — the DIRECT link to the architecture decision log. (Indirect links also exist via `finding_re… |
| `fitness_function_refs` | `array<ref → fitness_function_ref>` | — |  | Fitness functions (FF###) this intervention establishes or relies on as guardrails. |
| `migration_refs` | `array<ref → migration_ref>` | — |  | Migrations (MIG###) that implement the TO-BE change this intervention calls for. |
| `realized_by` | `array<ref → work_item_ref>` | — |  | Roadmap work-items (WI###) that deliver/sequence this intervention. Delivery is DELEGATED to the roadmap execution tier — leverage does not re-model steps/hori… |
| `advances_goals` | `array<ref → goal_ref>` | — |  | Motivation goals (G###) this intervention advances. |
| `advances_value_streams` | `array<ref → value_stream_ref>` | — |  | Value streams (VS###) / initiatives this intervention unblocks or accelerates. |
| `capability_refs` | `array<ref → capability_ref>` | — |  | Business capabilities (CAP###) this intervention strengthens. Optional. |
| `depends_on` | `array<ref → leverage_ref>` | — |  | Leverage points that must land first (prerequisites). Forms the leverage DAG. |
| `enables` | `array<ref → leverage_ref>` | — |  | Leverage points this one unblocks once done. Inverse edge of `depends_on`. |
| `consequences_if_done` | `array<string>` | — |  | What improves if this intervention is executed. |
| `consequences_if_not_done` | `array<string>` | — |  | What persists / degrades if it is NOT executed (the cost of inaction). |
| `discovery_stage` | `ref → discovery_stage` | — |  | Epistemic maturity of this leverage recommendation. |
| `certainty` | `ref → certainty` | — |  | Confidence in the recommendation (speculative \| probable \| confirmed). |
| `evidence` | `ref → evidence` | — |  | Evidence chain justifying the priority and the consequence framing. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Leverage-point version for lifecycle tracking. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Leverage-point ownership override. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/leverage.schema.yaml#/$defs/leverage_point`_

#### `watch_item`

A monitored signal not yet promoted to a leverage point. Links to the existing risk/finding it concerns rather than duplicating it.

**Required:** `id`, `title`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | ✓ |  | Local watch-item id (W + 3 digits). Not referenced elsewhere — local to this map. |

<a id="governance-motivation"></a>

### `governance/motivation.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Motivation**

Governance Plane: Strategic intent — goals, non-goals, risks, assumptions, and trade-offs. Decisions reference motivation entities (not reverse). Goals link forward to KPIs in quality.schema.yaml.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/motivation.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this motivation document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context this motivation file belongs to. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `goals` | `array<ref → goal>` | — |  | What the system aims to achieve. Goals drive decisions and prioritize work. Each goal can be tracked by a KPI in quality.schema.yaml. |
| `non_goals` | `array<ref → non_goal>` | — |  | Explicit exclusions — what the system intentionally does NOT do. Prevents scope creep and aligns stakeholder expectations. |
| `risks` | `array<ref → risk>` | — |  | Identified threats to the system's goals. Each risk has likelihood, impact, and mitigation. Risks drive defensive decisions. |
| `assumptions` | `array<ref → assumption>` | — |  | Things believed true but not yet verified. Wrong assumptions invalidate decisions. Each documents the consequence if false. |
| `trade_offs` | `array<ref → trade_off>` | — |  | Conscious compromises between competing concerns. Makes implicit architectural tension explicit with rationale. |
| `inquiries` | `array<ref → inquiry>` | — |  | Governance inquiries — unresolved strategic or stakeholder concerns that need investigation or decision before work can proceed. |

#### Definitions

#### `goal`

A strategic objective the system aims to achieve. Measurable goals link to KPIs; all goals drive decisions.

**Required:** `id`, `statement`, `priority`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → goal_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique goal identifier (G + NNN). |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description. |
| `statement` | `string` | ✓ |  | The goal as a clear, actionable statement (e.g. 'Reduce order processing time to under 2 seconds'). |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings. |
| `priority` | `string` | ✓ | `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` | Goal priority: critical=must have at launch, high=must have, medium=should have, low=nice to have. |
| `measure` | `string` | — |  | How achievement is measured (e.g. 'p95 latency < 200ms'). Link to kpi for formal tracking. |
| `kpi` | `ref → kpi_ref` | — |  | KPI in quality.schema.yaml that formally tracks this goal. Closes the goal→KPI→metric traceability chain. |
| `examples` | `array<object>` | — |  | Concrete examples illustrating this goal. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Goal version for lifecycle tracking. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Goal-level ownership override. |
| `discovery_stage` | `ref → discovery_stage` | — |  | Epistemic maturity of this goal. |
| `certainty` | `ref → certainty` | — |  | Confidence level of this goal assertion. |
| `evidence` | `ref → evidence` | — |  | Evidence justifying this goal's discovery_stage and certainty. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/motivation.schema.yaml#/$defs/goal`_

#### `non_goal`

An explicit exclusion — something the system intentionally does NOT do. Intentional boundary, not an oversight.

#### `risk`

An identified threat to the system's goals with probability, severity, and mitigation strategy.

Something believed to be true but not yet verified. Carries risk if wrong; consequence documents the exposure.

#### `work_item`

A roadmap work-breakdown node: an epic, phase, or foundation lane, or a nested subscope/task. Recursive via `children`. Placed by sprint (first-class, requires `cadence`) or by explicit date; rolls up to a milestone via `milestone`. Carries typed traceability to goals/risks/decisions/value-streams/stories/use-cases so delivery links back to strategic intent. Rendering concerns (colour, hatching,…

**Required:** `id`, `kind`, `name`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |

| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Short work-item title (e.g. 'Survey Setup', 'Reminders'). |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | What this work item delivers and why. |
| `status` | `string` | — | `planned`, `in-progress`, `achieved`, `deferred`, `cancelled` | Delivery lifecycle status (same axis as milestone.status). |
| `confidence` | `string` | — | `committed`, `estimated`, `tentative` | Planning confidence in the placement/scope — orthogonal to `status`. committed = firm dates; estimated = sized but movable; tentative = provisional/placeholder. |
| `progress` | `integer` | — |  | Percent complete (0–100). Rolls up (duration-weighted) to parents in a view. |
| `milestone` | `ref → milestone_ref` | — |  | The milestone (release) this work item rolls up to (e.g. the MVP milestone). |
| `start_sprint` | `number` | — |  | First sprint. Fractional allowed: 30.5 = halfway through sprint 30. Requires `cadence`. |
| `end_sprint` | `number` | — |  | End sprint. Integer = inclusive whole sprint; fractional (31.5) = that exact point. |

| `end_date` | `string` | — |  | Explicit end date (bar right edge). Overrides end_sprint when both are present. |

| `buffer_end` | `string` | — |  | Explicit buffer right edge. Overrides buffer_end_sprint. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Owning team/department/party (typed org reference). |

| `tracker_ref` | `string` | — |  | External issue-tracker key or URL (e.g. a Jira key 'ABC-1234'). The base URL / link construction is a view concern (Gantt view-config), not modelled here. |
| `note` | `string` | — |  | Free-text planning note (e.g. a scheduling caveat). |

| `use_cases` | `ref → use_case_ref_list` | — |  |  |

| `blockers` | `array<ref → blocker>` | — |  | Active blockers preventing progress. |
| `children` | `array<ref → work_item>` | — |  | Nested work items (e.g. an epic's subscopes; a subscope's tasks). |

| `assertion` | `string` | ✓ |  | The constraint expression to evaluate against the blueprint graph. |
| `severity` | `string` | — | `error`, `warning`, `info` | How to treat violations: error=block, warning=report, info=log. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |

| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

#### `test_case`

A single test case. Minimum: id, name, summary, validates.

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `validates`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → test_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique test ID. Prefix indicates suite: TC=happy-path, EC=edge-case, ER=error-case. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description. |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Human-readable scenario name (e.g. 'Submit order with valid items'). |
| `summary` | `string` | — |  | One-line summary for listings (≤200 chars). Self-contained. |
| `validates` | `ref → validates_refs` | ✓ |  | What this test proves. Authoritative source for test-to-blueprint traceability. |
| `version` | `ref → entity_version` | — |  | Test version for lifecycle tracking. |
| `given` | `ref → test_setup` | — |  | Initial state and preconditions (Arrange phase). |
| `expected_result` | `ref → expected_result` | — |  | Expected outcome (Assert phase). All fields optional — use what's relevant. |
| `note` | `string` | — |  | Additional context for test reviewers. Useful for non-obvious logic. |
| `golden_output` | `string` | — |  | Expected output as inline multiline content or a file path (e.g. ./golden/TC001.txt). Tooling determines interpretation. |
| `counter_example` | `object` | — |  | Documents what WRONG behavior looks like. Helps prevent future regressions from being mistaken for correct behavior. |
| `contract` | `object` | — |  | Contract evidence linking this test to a formal API contract. |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Test case-level ownership override. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

#### `validates_refs`

Typed references to blueprint entities this test validates. Tests OWN these links — authoritative for traceability.

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |

| `concepts` | `array<ref → concept_ref>` | — |  | Concepts this test verifies behavior of. |

| `questions` | `array<ref → question_ref>` | — |  | Questions this test validates the answer quality of. E.g., a test may verify that "What is the current order status?" is answered correctly under various condi… |
| `ownership` | `array<string>` | — |  | Org ownership refs (party, department, or team) this test validates. |

#### `test_setup`

Initial state and preconditions for the test (Arrange phase of Arrange-Act-Assert).

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | Human-readable description of the initial state. |

#### `expected_result`

Expected test outcome (Assert phase). Covers result codes, output assertions, format checks, and behavior.

| `code` | `integer` | — |  | Expected result code: CLI exit code (0=success) or HTTP status (200, 400, etc.). |

### `governance/value-stream.schema.yaml`

**Blueprint Value Streams**

Governance Plane: Value Stream Map — end-to-end flows of value delivery that cross-cut bounded contexts and capabilities. Value streams show HOW the business delivers outcomes, while capabilities show WHAT it can do.

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/value-stream.schema.yaml` · root type `object`_

**Root required:** `version`, `value_streams`

**Root properties:**

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `ref → semver` | ✓ |  | Content version of this value stream document. |
| `schemaVersion` | `ref → schema_version` | — |  | Schema version this document conforms to. Omit to assume latest. |
| `scope` | `ref → context_prefix` | — |  | Bounded context or business domain this value stream map covers. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | File-level ownership default. Entities inherit unless overridden. |
| `value_streams` | `array<ref → value_stream>` | ✓ |  | Value streams representing end-to-end flows of value delivery. |

#### Definitions

#### `value_stream`

An end-to-end flow of value delivery that crosses bounded contexts and capabilities. Stages represent ordered phases of value creation, each served by one or more capabilities.

**Required:** `id`, `name`, `stages`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `ref → value_stream_ref` | ✓ |  | Unique value stream identifier (VS001, VS002, etc.). |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Value stream name in business language. |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | What value this stream delivers and to whom. |
| `trigger` | `string` | — |  | What initiates this value stream (e.g., 'Customer searches for a product'). |
| `outcome` | `string` | — |  | The end value delivered (e.g., 'Customer receives purchased goods'). |
| `primary_actors` | `array<ref → actor_ref>` | — |  | Actors who initiate or benefit from this value stream. |
| `stages` | `array<ref → value_stream_stage>` | ✓ |  | Ordered phases of value creation within this stream. |
| `metrics` | `array<ref → kpi_ref>` | — |  | End-to-end KPIs measuring this value stream's effectiveness. |
| `goal_refs` | `array<ref → goal_ref>` | — |  | Strategic goals this value stream serves. |
| `discovery_stage` | `ref → discovery_stage` | — |  | Epistemic maturity of this value stream. |
| `certainty` | `ref → certainty` | — |  | Confidence level of this value stream definition. |
| `evidence` | `ref → evidence` | — |  | Evidence justifying this value stream's structure. |
| `tags` | `ref → tags` | — |  |  |
| `owned_by` | `ref → owned_by` | — |  | Value stream ownership override. |
| `properties` | `ref → entity_properties` | — |  |  |
| `code_refs` | `ref → code_refs` | — |  |  |

_Source: `schema/v2.7/governance/value-stream.schema.yaml#/$defs/value_stream`_

#### `value_stream_stage`

An ordered phase of value creation within a value stream.

**Required:** `name`, `capabilities`

| Property | Type | Req | Enum | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | ✓ |  | Stage name (e.g., 'Discover', 'Select', 'Purchase', 'Fulfill'). |
| `description` | `string` | — |  | What happens in this stage. |
| `capabilities` | `array<ref → capability_ref>` | ✓ |  | Capabilities that serve this stage. |
| `key_operations` | `array<ref → operation_ref>` | — |  | Highlight critical operations in this stage (optional convenience). |
| `actors` | `array<ref → actor_ref>` | — |  | Actors active in this stage. |
| `pain_points` | `array<string>` | — |  | Known friction points in this stage. |
| `lead_time` | `string` | — |  | Typical duration of this stage (e.g., '< 2 seconds', '1-3 business days'). |
